extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural guidance for a National Research Foundation and for Federal support of university, institute, and government research, including rules for fellowships, grants-in-aid, institutional accountability, coordination, and tax/patent environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional financial accountability and research committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The institution must be prepared to give a reasonable accounting of the expenditure of funds received and is to have a research committee, drawn preferably from the executive faculty and active investigators, which is to be informed on all local research expenditures and is to be responsible for the administration of the grant and for reports and accounting required by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research committee should administer the grant, oversee local expenditures, and ensure timely reports and accounting to the Foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Latitude in expenditure with periodic review and cancellation power
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions are to be allowed wide latitude in the expenditure of general research funds, but these expenditures are to be subject to review periodically by the Foundation, which is to have the power of cancellation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While institutions may manage funds broadly, the Foundation retains periodic review authority and may cancel funding for noncompliance or other reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of general research funds for junior fellowships (scope and restriction)
rubrics_metrics.description: General research funds may in part be used for junior fellowships to students working for an M.D. degree to permit recipients to devote 1 or 2 years full-time to acquiring more specialized knowledge of medical research techniques; junior fellowships are not to be used as scholarships to defray medical school tuition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should design junior fellowships to support full-time research training (1–2 years) and must not use these funds merely to cover tuition; overall fellowship policies (number, stipend value) are subject to Foundation review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for renewal discussions of general research funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal discussions concerning renewal of general research funds should be completed 1 to 3 years in advance of termination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan renewals well before end-date to ensure continuity and permit Foundation review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal right for refused applications (general research funds)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application for general research funds is refused, the applicant institution may appeal directly to the board of trustees for a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions have a formal appeal path directly to the Foundation's board of trustees when funding is denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation considerations for general research funds
rubrics_metrics.description: In allocating general research funds, the Foundation is to consider both the immediate needs and promise of development of the applicant institutions, and is to take cognizance of the effects of such funds upon the support of medical schools by their parent institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocation decisions should balance short-term needs and long-term development potential, and consider institutional ecosystems and parental support impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment ownership under block general research grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment purchased under general research funds is to become the property of the institution to which the block grant is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purchased equipment remains institutional property; plan acquisitions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship purpose and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are to be awarded by the Foundation for 1 to 3 years to approved applicants having the M.D., Ph.D., or D.D.S. degree or equivalent attainment to enable recipients to acquire research training, undertake research, learn special techniques, or pursue studies in related sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships target post-degree trainees to develop research capability, technique mastery, or related-science study over 1–3 year terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship selection criterion: potential for leadership vs past performance
rubrics_metrics.description: In the initial selection of Fellows, potentialities for development of leadership in medicine should be weighed as heavily as past performance in research work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection panels should value future leadership potential on par with demonstrated research achievements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowships not to substitute for residencies or primary postgraduate qualification
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships are not to be used to provide residencies, or primarily for obtaining postgraduate degrees or for qualifying for Certification by the Specialty Boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships must focus on research training and activity rather than clinical residency training or certification completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship training balance (teaching/clinical experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowships should include experience in teaching or the clinical care of patients, as these exercises are essential to balanced research training and imperative if a Fellow is to fit himself for maximal usefulness in medicine or the medical sciences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design fellowships to include some teaching or clinical responsibilities to ensure well-rounded research training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of fellowship stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellowship stipends are to be determined by the Foundation with due consideration of university salaries paid persons with equivalent training and experience, and to the desirability of encouraging relatively senior men to devote themselves to research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set stipends competitive with comparable university salaries and consider incentives to attract senior qualified researchers into research careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of fellows' research expenses and matched institutional benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Research expenses of a Fellow may be met by the Foundation. If an institution matches insurance or annuity payments by its faculty, a similar payment is to be added by the Foundation to the Fellow’s stipend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide for direct research costs and match institutional benefits where applicable to ensure equitable fellow support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship lapse on transfer without approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A fellowship is to lapse automatically if a Fellow transfers to another institution without approval by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows must obtain Foundation approval before institutional transfer or risk automatic termination of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants-in-aid term, purpose, and institutional endorsement
rubrics_metrics.description: Grants-in-aid extending for 1 to 10 years may be made to universities, medical schools, or other nonprofit scientific institutions for the support of specific projects or of specified investigators; applications for grants-in-aid are to carry the endorsement of the applicant institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grants-in-aid support project- or investigator-specific research for 1–10 years and require institutional endorsement at application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for renewal discussions of grants-in-aid
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal discussions concerning renewal should be completed prior to the beginning of the last third of the period of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiate renewal negotiations early—before the final third of the grant term—to ensure continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable overhead is reasonable but not automatic
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable overhead expenses may be included in the financial statement accompanying a request for a grant, but overhead payments are not to be automatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include overhead requests with justification; the Foundation will review and approve overhead selectively rather than as a routine add-on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements under grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports are to be submitted under each grant as required by the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with Foundation-specified reporting schedules and content as condition of funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment ownership under grant awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment purchased under a grant is to become the property of the institution to which the grant is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantee institutions hold title to equipment bought with grant funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal right for refused grants or extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request for a grant or for the extension of a grant is refused, the applicant institution may appeal directly to the board of trustees for a review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain institutional right to seek review by the Foundation's board when awards or extensions are denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation role in coordination and initiation of research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is to consider methods designed to stimulate research, to improve research conditions in institutions where it is now not well developed, to effect coordination among investigators working in a common field, and to facilitate publication, dissemination, and experimental application of scientific information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use funding and programmatic tools to stimulate underdeveloped research conditions, coordinate investigators, and promote dissemination and application of findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation should initiate/support but not itself conduct research
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is to initiate and support such new research work as may be indicated, but it is not itself to engage in research. Its integrative and catalytic efforts are to be carried out by recommendation and invitation rather than by direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act as catalytic funder and convener; avoid direct conduct of research or heavy-handed programmatic direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reporting by the Foundation to the President
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foundation is to report annually to the President, in the form he requests, on the progress of work carried out under its authority; with the President’s approval, all or part of the annual report is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce an annual report for the President, and publish content as authorized to ensure transparency and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter authority to modify procedures and experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: The authority to make and alter specific regulations and to experiment in procedures for fostering medical research is to be incorporated in the charter of the Foundation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embed flexible regulatory authority in the Foundation charter to allow experimentation and procedural adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope for Federal-conducted research (limits on expansion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research carried on directly by the Federal Government represents an important part of total research activity and needs to be strengthened and expanded after the war; expansion, however, should be limited to fields of inquiry and service which are of public importance and are not adequately carried on by private enterprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize Federal research in public-interest areas not sufficiently addressed by private sector to avoid unnecessary duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate civil service branch for scientific and technical positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate and distinct procedures for recruiting and classifying scientific personnel are warranted by the exacting technical requirements in these services; establish a separate branch of the Civil Service for scientific and technical positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement specialized recruitment/classification systems for scientific staff to improve quality of government research personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upgrade positions and salaries and select new talent carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: A general up-grading of positions and salaries in the scientific services of Government, accompanied by a careful selection of new talent, would be a major contribution to improvement of the quality of research conducted by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise compensation and refine hiring practices to attract and retain high-caliber scientific personnel in government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assured, long-run appropriations via lump sums for broad programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research programs of Government should be assured in terms of their long-run objectives; appropriations by Congress to the principal Government scientific departments should be made in lump sums for broad programs of research extending over several years, with annual budget allocations within the assured sum as at present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek multi-year lump-sum appropriations to provide program stability while retaining annual budgeting mechanisms for allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create a permanent science advisory board
rubrics_metrics.description: A permanent science advisory board should be created to consult with Government agencies and to advise the executive and legislative branches of government as to the policies and budgets of Government agencies engaged in scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish an ongoing advisory body to provide expert guidance on science policy and budgeting across government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tax and patent environment to encourage industrial research
rubrics_metrics.description: The structure of Federal taxation and the operation of the patent system have an important impact on the research and development policies of industry; in designing postwar taxes, consideration should be given to increasing incentives to industrial research and the proper treatment of research costs for tax purposes should receive clear legislative definition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tax and patent policies that incentivize industrial R&D and provide clear legislative rules for treatment of research expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of research types and institutional implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific research may be divided into pure research, background research, and applied research and development; each category requires different institutional arrangements for maximum development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize different research categories (pure/background/applied) when designing institutional support, governance, and funding mechanisms; e.g., pure research demands freedom of inquiry and sometimes shared expensive equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characteristics of pure research and public-domain expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Pure research is research without specific practical ends, resulting in general knowledge; it demands freedom of mind, may involve cooperative efforts and shared expensive equipment, and by general consent its discoveries have been consigned to the public domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect academic freedom for pure research and uphold norms of open dissemination; provide institutional arrangements that accommodate unpredictable, non-directed inquiry and shared infrastructure.
